summary: A photographer booked for a shoot (provider, under P2P and B2P), or booking someone such as a makeup artist for their own shoot (engager, under P2P). Draft wording for review; not legal advice.

clauses.text: [[Engager]] books as a working photographer, for a shoot that is part of their business.
[[Engager]] sends [[provider]] a brief for the shoot, with reference images where useful, at least {{brief_days}} days before it.
[[Engager]] directs the shoot and has the final say on the look of the images.
[[Engager]] confirms the venue, parking and access details to [[provider]] at least 48 hours before the shoot.
[[Engager]] gives [[provider]] a call sheet with the times for each part of the shoot.
[[Engager]] pays [[provider]] whether or not the images are later used or published.
[[Engager]] supplies the lighting, backdrops and space the shoot needs; [[provider]] brings the tools of their own trade.
[[Provider]] may use up to {{portfolio_count}} of the final images in their own portfolio once [[engager]] has published them, credited as “{{portfolio_credit}}”.
Copyright in the images belongs to [[engager]] as the photographer. [[Provider]] keeps any rights they have in their own designs.
[[Engager]] makes sure the set is safe, including lighting stands, cables and props, and tells [[provider]] about any hazard on arrival.
If [[engager]] moves the shoot with at least {{notice_hours}} hours’ notice, the booking moves to the new date without a cancellation charge if [[provider]] is free then.
[[Engager]] tells [[provider]] in advance if the shoot is confidential, for example an unreleased product, and what may not be shared.
[[Engager]] confirms through SnapLink, on the day, that [[provider]] attended and did the agreed work, or says what was not done.
[[Engager]] tells [[provider]] about any problem with their work during the shoot where possible, so it can be put right on the day.

Images the provider may use in their portfolio

clauses.text: [[Provider]] confirms that the portfolio on their SnapLink profile is their own work.
[[Provider]] delivers {{image_count}} edited images within {{delivery_days}} days of the shoot, by {{delivery_method}}.
[[Provider]] delivers the images without watermarks, at a resolution suitable for the licensed use.
[[Provider]] photographs every item on the shot list agreed before the shoot, or records on the day why an item could not be shot.
Editing means {{retouch_level}}. Further retouching is agreed and paid for separately.
[[Provider]] keeps a backup copy of the images until delivery and for at least {{archive_days}} days after it.
[[Provider]] may need up to 30 minutes at the venue before the start to set up, and [[engager]] arranges access for this.
[[Provider]] arrives at the venue ready to start by {{start_time}}.
In a shoot longer than six hours, [[provider]] takes a break of at least 20 minutes.
The fee covers the shoot, the editing and delivery of the agreed number of images, and the licence in this agreement.
[[Provider]] brings working camera equipment to the shoot, with spare batteries and memory cards.
Prints, albums, extra edited images and props are not included unless this agreement lists them.
[[Engager]] may use the delivered images in {{usage_media}}, in {{usage_territory}}, for {{usage_term}} from delivery. Each published use carries the credit “{{credit_line}}” where the medium allows.

[[Engager]] may use the delivered images for their own private and domestic purposes, including sharing them with family and friends and on personal social media. Commercial use needs a separate licence.
The licence is non-exclusive and cannot be passed on to anyone else without [[provider]]’s written consent.
[[Provider]] keeps copyright in every image, including images not delivered. Raw files are not handed over.
[[Provider]] asserts the right to be identified as the author of the images.
[[Provider]] holds public liability insurance and shows the certificate on request.
If drone photography is agreed, [[provider]] holds the operator and flyer registrations the Civil Aviation Authority requires and flies within its rules.

If [[provider]] cannot attend because of illness or an emergency, they tell [[engager]] at once and try to offer a suitably experienced replacement photographer. [[Engager]] may accept the replacement or cancel for a full refund.

Because [[engager]] commissioned these photographs for private and domestic purposes, [[provider]] will not show them in public, publish them or use them in a portfolio without [[engager]]’s written consent.
[[Provider]] may use up to {{portfolio_count}} of the delivered images in their own portfolio and promotion, unless [[engager]] asks otherwise before signing.
[[Provider]] respects any request from a person at the shoot not to be photographed, and [[engager]] tells [[provider]] in advance about anyone who has asked.
Where [[engager]] supplies models, products or locations, [[engager]] is responsible for having the consents and permissions needed to photograph them.
Delivery of the gallery with the agreed number of edited images shows that the main duty was done; SnapLink records the delivery date.
[[Engager]] raises any complaint about the images within 14 days of delivery where they can, naming the images concerned, so that [[provider]] can re-edit them first.
